evals.prompt: Add an 'Add Note' button to PersonDetailView. Clicking it opens a small modal form with a single textarea where the user can type a note. On submit it calls window.api.persons.update(id, { notes }) and closes the modal. The button should be in the existing notes section of PersonDetailView.
evals.expected_output: A Vue component or inline addition that uses <BaseModal> (not raw div.modal-overlay), uses useToast for the catch block, uses $t() for all button labels and placeholder text, uses var(--color-*) CSS variables for any scoped styles, and does NOT have a local 'declare const window' block.
assertions: Uses <BaseModal> component, not a raw div with class modal-overlay
Imports and calls useToast for error handling in the save catch block
Has NO local 'declare const window' type declaration
All user-visible strings (button labels, placeholder, heading) use $t() not hardcoded text
Any scoped CSS uses var(--color-*) or var(--font-*) variables, not hardcoded hex values

evals.prompt: Create a new PersonCitationsSection.vue component. It should self-load all citations for a person (using window.api.citations.forPerson), display them in a table with source title and page columns, and be reusable in both PersonDetailView and PersonPanel. Follow the established Person Section Component pattern.
evals.expected_output: A self-loading Vue component using watch(() => props.personId, load, { immediate: true }) instead of onMounted, with useToast for error handling, no local declare const window, $t() for all visible strings, and CSS variables for any scoped styles.
assertions: Uses watch(() => props.personId, load, { immediate: true }) to load data, NOT onMounted
Has NO local 'declare const window' type declaration
Imports and calls useToast; catch block calls toast.error(t('errors.loadFailed')) or equivalent
All user-visible strings use $t() not hardcoded Swedish or English text
Any scoped CSS uses var(--color-*) or var(--font-*) variables, not hardcoded hex values like #2c3e50 or #333

evals.prompt: Add a living/deceased status badge to the person rows in PersonsView. Living persons should show a green 'Living' badge and deceased persons a gray 'Deceased' badge. Style the badges inline in the component's scoped styles.
evals.expected_output: Badge styling that uses CSS variables (var(--color-*)) instead of hardcoded hex colors, and badge label text that uses $t() not hardcoded strings.
assertions: Badge background and text colors use var(--color-*) CSS variables, not hardcoded hex values
Badge label strings ('Living', 'Deceased' or Swedish equivalents) use $t() not hardcoded text
Has NO local 'declare const window' type declaration
Does NOT redefine shared classes like .btn-add, .data-table, or .clickable-row in scoped styles
